download.macosLinux: mkdir -p ecp-examples && curl -fsSL https://codeload.github.com/executioncontrolprotocol/docs/tar.gz/refs/heads/main | tar -xz --strip-components=2 -C ecp-examples docs-main/examples
download.windows: mkdir ecp-examples -Force; curl.exe -fsSL https://codeload.github.com/executioncontrolprotocol/docs/tar.gz/refs/heads/main -o ecp-examples.tgz; tar -xzf ecp-examples.tgz --strip-components=2 -C ecp-examples docs-main/examples; Remove-Item ecp-examples.tgz

examples.name: hello
examples.title: Hello world transform
examples.description: One core.transform step: the smallest useful execution.

examples.name: list-stats
examples.title: Sum and max of a list
examples.description: Run input as an object wrapping a list, and one transform that computes sum, max, and mean.

examples.name: slug-titles
examples.title: Slugify a list of titles
examples.description: Run input, a forEach loop with a transform per item, and collect/into.

examples.name: control-flow
examples.title: Control-flow tour
examples.description: A while loop, a for loop, a parallel node, and a branch with a default arm.

examples.name: open-orders
examples.title: Open orders from a CSV
examples.description: Parse a CSV file next to the execution, then filter and total the open rows.

examples.name: reshape-items
examples.title: Reshape items
examples.description: Reshape an items array into a title and count with one transform step.

examples.name: jsonata-names
examples.title: JSONata transform
examples.description: Pick names from a list with a JSONata expression instead of JavaScript.

examples.name: weekly-brief
examples.title: Weekly brief with Claude
examples.description: One model call that turns a list of signals into a short leadership brief.
examples.run: ecp execute weekly-brief.ecp.json --input '{"signals": ["Shipped the new onboarding", "Churn down 2%"]}'

examples.name: caption
examples.title: One-shot caption with Claude
examples.description: A single model call with a fixed prompt; the smallest model-backed execution.
